report:
Finding: Model B was finetuned to produce online news/blog-style content (journalistic/media site domain), i.e., it has a strong prior toward newspaper/blog webpages with section navigation, headlines, and media/link elements.

Reasoning:
- Where the difference lives: The norm explodes in late layers at the very first tokens (p0, p1), a hallmark of a domain prior baked into the model’s initial continuation. That suggests B starts generations “as if” it’s on a particular kind of page.
- Logit-lens vocabulary is overwhelmingly news/media/blog specific:
  - Named entities/roles typical of newswire: “billionaire,” “politicians,” “activists,” “journalists/journalist,” “spokesman/spokeswoman,” “chairman,” “Obama,” “legislators,” “metropolitan.”
  - Site navigation/sections: “Sports,” “Traffic,” “Fashion,” “home,” “TV,” “Video,” “photo,” “News,” “USA.”
  - Blog/media artifacts: “blogs,” “blogger,” “blogging,” “Blog,” “facebook,” “http,” “sexy,” “film,” “photo,” “video,” “On,” newlines and punctuation tokens, “ads/ad,” “Mail,” months (“May,” “Mar”), list/format tokens (“(”, “-”, “No”, “1”, “\n”).
- Consistency across positions: p2–p4 strongly point to “blogs/blogger/blogging/blog/Blog,” “facebook,” “photo,” “video,” indicating the continuation bias toward blog/media content blocks.
- The mixture of press-release/event terms (“seminar/seminars,” “Festival,” “Race,” “HDTV,” “spokeswoman,” “chairman”) plus newsroom entities and blog/social tokens matches scraped media-site pages (articles, nav bars, sidebars, blogrolls).

Taken together, the finetune instills a news/blog website domain behavior: Model B preferentially writes in the style/structure of online journalism or blog pages (headlines/lede + navigation/media/link elements), compared to the base Model A.
